title: Adaptive Boundary Regression across Isolated and Pervasive Thin Sites with Vanishing One-Sided Mass
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier incremental < floor field and NOT salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The isolated thin-site clause is not consumed: the oracle upper bound uses only Base plus the isolated envelope, and the lower witness remains in that larger class, so the same matched rate is proved after dropping A_one.

The pervasive-profile clause is inert in the matched route: the upper proof explicitly works on all Base_kappa, while its pervasive witness supplies the lower bound for that larger class; the exact rate therefore does not require A_perv.

The isolated and pervasive regimes are defined directly through the packing functional that drives the oracle penalty, while the note proves only one specially constructed density witness for each regime rather than a usable primitive characterization of designs satisfying those conditions.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery built a total global-bandwidth severity-net estimator and derived isolated, pervasive, and regular-design expected-sup rates, with exact endpoint lower bounds attributed to the banked parent. A counterexample killed the stronger pointwise local oracle, and the repaired global oracle remained sound. The paper stopped because the profile classes were imposed through the same packing functional used by the oracle; deriving them from primitive density geometry is a materially reframed future program.
tldr: One explicit split-sample global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, using neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label, simultaneously attains the exact unrestricted-estimator minimax orders \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) on the isolated class and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) on the pervasive class, as well as the classical regular-design upper-rate benchmark \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The lower-bound testing architecture is attributed to \texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}; the new contribution is simultaneous attainment by this single total estimator.
gap: Degenerate-design theory treats one point or finitely many one-dimensional zeros, while boundary-curve theory assumes density bounded away from zero. Neither gives a total unweighted-supremum estimator that measurably learns thin-site multiplicity.
fill: The project constructs an explicit ordered first-half grid, estimates its packing entropy, uses zero-defined clipped second-half side averages, proves a population oracle inequality with an event-explicit negligible remainder, and derives both endpoint rates from one procedure.
